subject: general
question: In which of the following Articles the concept of equality is enshrined?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 14** of the Indian Constitution enshrines the concept of equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• It is a fundamental right that ensures that no person is discriminated against by the state on arbitrary grounds.
 
• This article is a cornerstone of the Indian legal system, providing a basis for challenging unjust laws and actions of the state.
 
• Article 14 is part of the larger framework of fundamental rights that are guaranteed to all citizens of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14** is part of Part III of the Indian Constitution, which deals with fundamental rights.
 
• Equality before the law means that every individual, regardless of their status, is subject to the same laws and can seek the same legal protections.
 
• Equal protection of the laws means that individuals in similar circumstances should be treated alike by the law.
 
• The Constitution of India guarantees several other fundamental rights, including the right to freedom (Articles 19-22), the right against exploitation (Articles 23-24), and the right to constitutional remedies (Article 32).
 
• Article 14 is often invoked in cases of discrimination, arbitrary state action, and to ensure fairness in administrative and legislative actions.
 
• Judicial interpretations of Article 14 have expanded its scope to include various dimensions of equality, including substantive equality and non-arbitrariness.
